correctness.rationale: While there has been no failure, occupied spaces are an interval about m. Until the left side fills, the next left vacancy is at distance L+1 when L places on the left are filled; the backward move therefore tracks the recurrence for b exactly up to that cap. If car i is first to fail, all n−m right spaces are occupied, L<m−1, and b_i=L. Since i−2=L+n−m, even an increment at every remaining index gives b_n≤L+n−i=m−2. Conversely, complete success fills all m−1 left places and has achieved that level. Recording the increment indices yields the threshold subsequence, and any witness subsequence forces the greedy score to reach each threshold by the corresponding index. Each elementary vector is feasible because i_j≥j+1, and the vectors have different equal-size supports, so none dominates another. The union of their principal upsets is precisely the success set. Each vector has the stated total quota. Inserting the new maximum into the k descent gaps or the final gap preserves k descents; the other gaps add one. The two ordered gap lists match the two quota ranges, and deletion uniquely reverses each step. This proves both the bijection and Eulerian tail, including the all-success case m=1, n=1, and the single maximal-threshold strategy at m=n. The recorded finite enumeration is corroboration only.
residual_risks: For arbitrary preference vectors the interval invariant need not hold; no extension to those vectors is being validated.

evidence: Theorem 4.2 realizes principal upsets by a preference chosen from a supplied strategy, not by determining the upset for a fixed unanimous preference. The §5 opening and §8 distinguish the unsolved general antichain question from the solved total-quota problem. The earlier paper uses a common fixed backward bound.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Upward closure and principal-upset realizability do not classify the generators for this fixed preference. A bound shared by all cars cannot enumerate their independent quotas.

evidence: For unanimous preference the excess interval is [2,m] with excess j−1 at j. Specializing the nested sets in Theorem 5.4 gives exactly positive quotas 1,…,m−1 on an increasing set of m−1 post-first car indices, zero elsewhere.
The frozen interval proof shows every successful strategy dominates one of these vectors, not just that they minimize total quota.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A total-quota minimizer is componentwise minimal, but a componentwise-minimal element may have larger total quota. The special-case domination argument closes that gap and enables the independent Eulerian enumeration; it is not implied by listing the minimizers.

originality.rationale: Ferrari–Verciani already give exactly these minimum-total profiles, their quota totals and their binomial count in the unanimous specialization. The supported contribution is showing that there are no additional componentwise-minimal successful profiles, giving an explicit threshold test for the whole upset, and obtaining the Eulerian-tail success count and a compatible permutation encoding. Neither the original model nor the Eulerian recurrence is claimed as new.
residual_risks: The indexed comparisons do not exhaust parking or inversion-sequence literature.
No claim is made that the custom insertion map is the usual inversion-sequence encoding or that no other Eulerian statistic can be identified with this greedy statistic.

value.rationale: Unanimous preferences provide a natural nontrivial class for the stated unresolved general antichain problem. The new exclusion of all other componentwise minima gives an exact description of a successful upset that can have exponentially many generators. The greedy score also converts every successful-strategy count in the class to a classical permutation distribution instead of enumerating its elements or reasoning just about quota minimizers.
residual_risks: The combinatorial identification is for the unanimous case; no prediction of the antichain or enumeration for other preferences follows.
